purpose: Present every semantic-surviving assessment candidate in one human review packet before any published-case change.
promotion_boundary: Packet generation is read-only with respect to the published case manifest. Every item starts pending_human_review. A separate explicit human decision and a reviewed repository change are required to publish a case.
review_rule: Confirm the candidate adds a materially new Lead reasoning signal.
Confirm expected points match the requested reasoning level rather than only topic knowledge.
Confirm evidence and human references support the load-bearing SAP facts or clearly mark author heuristics.
Confirm closest published cases do not make the candidate redundant.
Confirm red flags, follow-ups, and proof requirements are useful for an actual oral assessment.
Decide approve, revise, or reject explicitly; no missing decision is treated as approval.

items.title: The agent selects the wrong SAP object or writes incorrect fields through an MCP tool
items.prompt: Synthetic assessment candidate. The agent selects the wrong SAP object or writes incorrect fields through an MCP tool. Build a Lead-level diagnosis. Find the first wrong layer, explain ownership, and define evidence that proves the cause before correction.
expected_points: Start from the documented symptom and define the expected business state before changing downstream data or documents.
Use the first evidence checks before correction: tool contract, semantic context, input schema.
Continue the hypothesis tree with: business-key resolution, write validation.
Name the owner of the first wrong layer and separate that responsibility from teams that only see the downstream symptom.
Define proof of cause and proof of business completion before closing the case.
follow_up_questions: Which check would most quickly separate the root cause from a downstream symptom?
What evidence would prove the business process is complete after the fix?
red_flags: Do not repair the final symptom before proving the root cause.
Repairs the downstream symptom before proving the first wrong state.

semantic_review.reason: The candidate tests a distinct AI/Data diagnostic path. The published AI diagnosis case focuses on trajectory, permissions, and approval bypass after a risky agent path. RAW-MCP instead asks whether the selected SAP capability and write payload are semantically correct: tool contract, semantic context, input schema, business-key resolution, and backend write validation.
semantic_review.novel_signal: Tool access can be technically valid while the selected business capability, key, or field semantics are wrong.
review_checks: Keep the case focused on tool semantics and business-key resolution rather than generic prompt quality.
Require the learner to separate MCP/tool discovery from the business contract of the SAP capability.
Require proof in the authoritative SAP object after correction, not only a successful tool response.

items.title: Error is visible but no team owns correction or business confirmation
items.prompt: Synthetic assessment candidate. Error is visible but no team owns correction or business confirmation. Build a Lead-level diagnosis. Find the first wrong layer, explain ownership, and define evidence that proves the cause before correction.
expected_points: Start from the documented symptom and define the expected business state before changing downstream data or documents.
Use the first evidence checks before correction: interface recipient, business owner, technical owner.
Continue the hypothesis tree with: master-data/config owner, severity/SLA, runbook escalation.
Name the owner of the first wrong layer and separate that responsibility from teams that only see the downstream symptom.
Define proof of cause and proof of business completion before closing the case.
follow_up_questions: Which check would most quickly separate the root cause from a downstream symptom?
What evidence would prove the business process is complete after the fix?
red_flags: Do not make middleware operations the default owner for every receiver application error.
Repairs the downstream symptom before proving the first wrong state.

semantic_review.reason: Published Integration Operations cases test commit state, retry/idempotency, ordering, master-data failure, duplicate consumers, and an operational scorecard. This candidate is a Diagnose case about a different failure: the error is visible, but ownership of correction and business confirmation is undefined. It requires separating technical recipient ownership, business-state ownership, master-data/configuration ownership, SLA/runbook responsibility, and final reconciliation.
semantic_review.novel_signal: An observable integration error is not operationally controlled until correction ownership and business-confirmation ownership are explicit.
review_checks: Keep the case diagnostic: find the first missing ownership contract, not design a generic monitoring dashboard.
Require separate owners for technical correction and business confirmation when they differ.
Reject a rewrite that becomes only a KPI/scorecard design case already covered by ASSESS-INTOPS-006.

items.title: Production is finished but stock or warehouse receipt is missing or wrong
items.prompt: Synthetic assessment candidate. Production is finished but stock or warehouse receipt is missing or wrong. Build a Lead-level diagnosis. Find the first wrong layer, explain ownership, and define evidence that proves the cause before correction.
expected_points: Start from the documented symptom and define the expected business state before changing downstream data or documents.
Use the first evidence checks before correction: order and delivery-completed status, goods-receipt relevance, quantity and UoM.
Continue the hypothesis tree with: storage/batch/quality context, automatic versus manual GR, EWM inbound flow where used.
Name the owner of the first wrong layer and separate that responsibility from teams that only see the downstream symptom.
Define proof of cause and proof of business completion before closing the case.
follow_up_questions: Which check would most quickly separate the root cause from a downstream symptom?
What evidence would prove the business process is complete after the fix?
red_flags: Do not mark the order complete while the inventory event remains unexplained.
Repairs the downstream symptom before proving the first wrong state.

semantic_review.reason: A missing or wrong finished-goods receipt is a distinct completion boundary. Existing Production practice covers component staging and production structure, while the finance case starts after a finished product was received. A dedicated case can test whether the learner separates confirmation, inventory receipt, warehouse inbound flow, quality/batch context, and valuation.
semantic_review.novel_signal: Production progress is not proof that the intended finished-product inventory event occurred.
review_checks: Keep the symptom at the Production to Inventory/EWM boundary.
Require proof of order quantity, GR relevance, storage/batch/quality context, automatic versus manual GR, and warehouse flow where used.
Do not turn the case into a generic inventory-posting question.

items.title: MRP creates too much, too little, or repeated production supply
items.prompt: Synthetic assessment candidate. MRP creates too much, too little, or repeated production supply. Build a Lead-level diagnosis. Find the first wrong layer, explain ownership, and define evidence that proves the cause before correction.
expected_points: Start from the documented symptom and define the expected business state before changing downstream data or documents.
Use the first evidence checks before correction: requirement quantity and date, stock and existing receipts, planning strategy.
Continue the hypothesis tree with: lot sizing, safety stock or planning parameters, procurement type.
Name the owner of the first wrong layer and separate that responsibility from teams that only see the downstream symptom.
Define proof of cause and proof of business completion before closing the case.
follow_up_questions: Which check would most quickly separate the root cause from a downstream symptom?
What evidence would prove the business process is complete after the fix?
red_flags: Do not resize the planned order before reconstructing the net requirement.
Repairs the downstream symptom before proving the first wrong state.

semantic_review.reason: The failure starts before production-order execution: MRP creates an incorrect supply quantity from demand, stock, lot sizing, planning strategy, or planning parameters. The current Production cases cover production model choice, production-method structure, component staging, and cross-process finance, but not a dedicated net-requirement quantity diagnosis.
semantic_review.novel_signal: Reconstruct net requirement and planning inputs before resizing a planned order.
review_checks: Keep the case focused on why MRP created the quantity, not on generic MRP explanation.
Require evidence for requirement quantity/date, stock and receipts, lot sizing, safety stock/planning parameters, and procurement type.
Reject any final wording that can be answered by listing MRP configuration without reconstructing the net requirement.

items.title: Choose the supply model for a new customer offering
items.prompt: A company launches a configurable product with uncertain demand. Some customers need short lead times, some orders require customer-specific production, and an external supplier can also deliver the product. Design the sales-to-supply model. Compare sell-from-stock, make-to-order, and third-party supply before selecting the default and exception paths.
expected_points: Start from customer promise, demand variability, customization, stock risk, and supplier capability rather than from a sales document type.
Compare sell-from-stock, make-to-order, and third-party supply as different ownership models for inventory, supply execution, and customer commitment.
Explain which master-data and process decisions must distinguish the variants and where Sales hands responsibility to Production or Procurement.
Include ATP/customer-promise implications, billing path, inventory ownership, and the financial consequence of the selected supply model.
Define a default model plus explicit exception criteria instead of forcing every order through one variant.
Name the trade-off between response time, working capital, customization, supplier dependency, and process complexity, then state what condition would change the choice.
follow_up_questions: What would make you move a product from make-to-order to stock-based fulfillment?
Which responsibility remains with Sales in a third-party flow even when Procurement owns supplier execution?
red_flags: Chooses a process variant from SAP familiarity before stating the business operating model.
Treats third-party, make-to-order, and stock sales as document-type differences only.
Does not state what condition would change the design.

semantic_review.reason: The existing Sales Design case diagnoses ownership and customer promise in a chosen third-party flow, while the MTO Design case explains one customer-specific production model. This candidate asks the learner to choose among stock, make-to-order, and third-party operating models before configuration, define a default plus exceptions, and state the business condition that changes the design. The decision signal is materially broader and different.
semantic_review.novel_signal: Select the sales-to-supply operating model from business constraints and explicit decision-changing conditions before choosing SAP process controls.
review_checks: Keep at least three viable supply alternatives in the prompt.
Require a default model plus exception criteria rather than a generic pros-and-cons list.
Require ownership and downstream ATP, inventory, billing, production/procurement, and finance consequences.
Reject a rewrite that becomes a third-party troubleshooting case or a pure MTO explanation.

items.title: Invoice quantity or source relationship is wrong
items.prompt: Synthetic assessment candidate. Invoice quantity or source relationship is wrong. Build a Lead-level diagnosis. Find the first wrong layer, explain ownership, and define evidence that proves the cause before correction.
expected_points: Start from the documented symptom and define the expected business state before changing downstream data or documents.
Use the first evidence checks before correction: reference document and item, copying control, billing quantity rule.
Continue the hypothesis tree with: partial billing history, document flow.
Name the owner of the first wrong layer and separate that responsibility from teams that only see the downstream symptom.
Define proof of cause and proof of business completion before closing the case.
follow_up_questions: Which check would most quickly separate the root cause from a downstream symptom?
What evidence would prove the business process is complete after the fix?
red_flags: Do not correct the invoice amount before proving which quantity is actually billable.
Repairs the downstream symptom before proving the first wrong state.

semantic_review.reason: The published Billing cases cover due-state, split, repricing, FI transfer/account determination, external invoice delivery, and correction lifecycle. This candidate instead asks why billing quantity or value follows an unexpected predecessor relationship. The Lead signal is to reconstruct the reference document, copy-control path, source quantity/value, and billing relationship before changing pricing or the invoice manually.
semantic_review.novel_signal: Prove the billing reference and copy-control relationship before repairing a downstream quantity or value symptom.
review_checks: Keep the first diagnostic branch on source document relationship and copied quantity/value, not generic billing troubleshooting.
Require document flow and copy-control evidence before any pricing or manual billing correction.
Reject a rewrite that collapses into not-billing-due or repricing behavior already covered by published cases.
